description: Fields from competitors/findings.jsonl that the contract has no place for, keyed by contract record_id / claim_id. Not read by the team validator or exporter.

luis:us_mercedes-F0070.statement: Reviewer finds the E350's 255-hp 2.0-liter mild-hybrid powertrain silky and adequately powerful for the car's purpose.

luis:us_mercedes-F0071.statement: Reviewer states the optional adaptive air suspension soaks up potholes and expansion joints without losing body control.

luis:us_mercedes-F0072.statement: Reviewer finds the brakes touchy, sometimes causing a sudden lurch that surprised passengers.

luis:us_mercedes-F0073.statement: Reviewer praises the optional Superscreen's graphics, processing speed and animations; the passenger screen streams video and goes private while driving.

luis:us_mercedes-F0074.statement: Reviewer praises the cabin's gloss-black, frosted-aluminum and dark-wood trim and the rich optional leather.

luis:us_mercedes-F0075.statement: Reviewer suspects the screen-heavy cockpit, aimed at younger buyers, may not appeal to traditional Mercedes buyers.

luis:us_mercedes-F0076.statement: Reviewer warns that options and packages add up quickly; the loaded test car reached $82,000 against a $63,450 base price.

luis:us_mercedes-F0145.statement: Reviewer states the narrow rear window limits the view behind and the tall dashboard hurts forward visibility.

luis:us_mercedes-F0146.statement: Reviewer states the low roofline and raised rear cushions put rear passengers' heads against the headliner and make getting in and out awkward.

luis:us_mercedes-F0147.statement: Reviewer finds the 12.8-inch portrait touchscreen tricky to navigate at a glance; it takes many exposures to learn.

luis:us_mercedes-F0148.statement: Reviewer states the digital gauge cluster sits so high that he had to raise the steering wheel and drive with his arms up.

luis:us_mercedes-F0149.statement: Reviewer states the driver-monitoring camera repeatedly asked him to raise the steering wheel, and raising the seat was not possible because of limited headroom under the panoramic roof.

luis:us_mercedes-F0150.statement: Reviewer praises the ride for soaking up bumps.

luis:us_mercedes-F0151.statement: Reviewer finds the cabin very quiet, with little tire, motor or wind noise.

luis:us_mercedes-F0152.statement: Reviewer praises the agility from rear-wheel steering of up to 10 degrees, although steering feel is numb.

luis:us_mercedes-F0153.statement: Reviewer criticizes a dead, uncommunicative brake pedal; with strong regen the pedal moves on its own when lifting off the accelerator.

luis:us_mercedes-F0154.statement: Reviewer criticizes the tall, cliff-like dashboard, especially with the optional Hyperscreen.

luis:us_premium_others-F0217.statement: Reviewer praises the new 12.3-in touchscreen, moved 4.3 in closer to the driver, which replaces the old non-touch display that was hard to use while driving.

luis:us_premium_others-F0218.statement: Reviewer likes that Apple CarPlay can use the full 12.3-in screen.

luis:us_premium_others-F0219.statement: Reviewer praises the comfort and refinement of the ES 350 V6 on the standard suspension.

luis:us_premium_others-F0220.statement: Reviewer welcomes Lexus Safety System+ 2.5 making blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert standard, plus intersection turning assist.

luis:us_premium_others-F0221.statement: Reviewer notes the V6 ES 350 starts at the same price as the four-cylinder ES 250 ($41,875 incl. destination).

luis:us_premium_others-F0222.statement: Reviewer states the backup and 360-degree camera images are distorted and less clear than they should be.

luis:us_premium_others-F0223.statement: Reviewer states lane centering holds its position inconsistently, tending to drift to the right.

luis:us_premium_others-F0224.statement: Reviewer finds the F Sport package rides harsher even with adjustable shocks, and its handling gains are not worth the cost.

luis:us_premium_others-F0225.statement: Reviewer argues the front-drive-only ES 350 V6 needs all-wheel drive, which is offered only on the ES 250.

luis:us_premium_others-F0323.statement: Cars.com editors list Super Cruise hands-free driver assistance as a strength of the 2025 CT5.

luis:us_premium_others-F0324.statement: Cars.com editors list the roomy cabin as a strength.

luis:us_premium_others-F0325.statement: Cars.com editors list the ride quality as a strength.

luis:us_premium_others-F0326.statement: Cars.com editors list the new 2025 tech features, including the 33-in display, as a strength.

luis:us_premium_others-F0327.statement: Cars.com editors praise the ferocious acceleration of the CT5-V Blackwing.

luis:us_premium_others-F0328.statement: Cars.com editors find acceleration only so-so with the base turbo four-cylinder.

luis:us_premium_others-F0329.statement: Cars.com editors list the cozy trunk as a weakness.

luis:us_premium_others-F0330.statement: Cars.com editors find back-seat headroom tight for tall adults.

luis:us_premium_others-F0331.statement: Cars.com editors find the interior materials not as upscale as many rivals'.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0090.statement: Reviewer finds the Long Range's acceleration smooth and quite strong.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0091.statement: Reviewer states the overhauled suspension gives ride and handling that rival a German sports sedan.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0092.statement: Reviewer notes a quieter cabin thanks to added sound deadening and acoustic glass.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0093.statement: Reviewer praises the Supercharger experience; Tesla claims up to 185 miles added in about 15 minutes.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0094.statement: Reviewer reports the touch-sensitive turn-signal pad sometimes did not work and was easy to press by mistake.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0095.statement: Reviewer warns the touchscreen gear selector could be a deal breaker for some buyers; redundant headliner shift buttons act as a backup.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0096.statement: Reviewer prefers physical controls to the mostly digital ones and finds the UI restrictive.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0097.statement: Reviewer notes meaningful materials upgrades, such as textured cloth replacing the wood veneer.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0098.statement: Reviewer states the car feels like good value for the money.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0211.statement: Reviewer finds the dual-motor A6 (456 hp, 0-60 mph in 4.3 s) properly quick, though the S6 does not feel much stronger.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0212.statement: Reviewer praises the well-balanced ride on the available adaptive air suspension, comparing it to flying rather than driving.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0213.statement: Reviewer finds the car nearly as good in corners as the gas S6.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0214.statement: Reviewer finds the steering light and obviously digital, and says the car is not meant to excite.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0215.statement: Reviewer praises the strong, impressive braking.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0216.statement: Reviewer likes the four regen levels set with steering-wheel paddles, ranging from near one-pedal driving to almost no regen.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0217.statement: Reviewer calls the MMI one of the nicer and easier systems to operate: clear, intuitive and responsive.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0218.statement: Reviewer notes the only physical controls are a volume knob, a start button and a short rocker shifter, which makes the cabin feel clinical.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0219.statement: Reviewer notes the usual luxury materials, such as leather, with microsuede accents in the S6.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0220.statement: Reviewer criticizes lofty pricing and too little difference between the A6 and the S6, which costs about $10,800 more than the dual-motor A6.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0247.statement: Reviewer (Prestige with Sport Plus) finds the standard 362-hp V6 powerful and Audi's 4.5 s 0-60 mph claim believable.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0248.statement: Reviewer finds the seven-speed dual-clutch transmission shifts smoothly.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0249.vfc_level2: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology
luis:us_tesla_audi-F0249.statement: Reviewer finds the car not particularly thrilling or fun to drive, with a bit less emotional warmth than before.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0250.statement: Reviewer praises the ride quality and finds the adaptive air suspension rides better than the Sport Plus setup.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0251.statement: Reviewer finds the Sport Plus package adds only moderate agility over the standard A6, with cornering ability well beyond what typical buyers need.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0252.statement: Reviewer calls the MMI interface one of the best in the industry, with an extensive screen setup.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0253.statement: Reviewer dislikes the heavy use of gloss-black surfaces; the page's cons list says the interior feels cheap in places.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0254.statement: Reviewer calls the roughly $6,000 rise in base price over the previous model steep, though standard equipment has increased.
